newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-GREENE CLOCKS QUICKEST TIME IN 100 SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GREENE CLOCKS QUICKEST TIME IN 100 SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Maurice Greene headed the field into the world championships 100 metres final on Sunday when he clocked his fourth successive run of 9.90 seconds to defeat defending champion Donovan Bailey in their semifinal.

American champion Greene and Bailey, running in adjacent lanes, eyeballed each other as they crossed the line, with Bailey, showing no ill-effects from the cramp which seemed to affect him in the opening rounds on Saturday, clocking 9.91 seconds.
It was the fastest time of the year for the Canadian Olympic champion and world record holder.

Namibian Frankie Fredericks (9.93) and American Tim Montgomery (10.08) also made it through to Sunday night's final which will feature five men who contested last year's Olympic final in Atlanta -- Bailey and Fredericks from that heat, and Ato Boldon, Davidson Ezinwa and Mike Marsh from the first semifinal.
Trinidad's Boldon, running with almost contemptuous ease, breezed into the final with an effortless win in an even 10 seconds which inspired a rare joke from stadium announcer Bob Sparks.
"The winner was Ato Boldon, almost becoming the first athlete to clock 10.00 seconds for the 100 metres running backwards," Sparks said.
Ezinwa was second in 10.15, followed by Marsh (10.21) and Bruny Surin of Canada, fourth in 10.22.
Boldon said: "At 75 metres I looked around and it was way too early. It was a rookie mistake. We might have had a world record if the weather hadn't changed. It's cooler. It's nasty out there."
Greene disagreed: "It was easy, its fine. The record is gone."
A defiant Bailey, written off by many observers following his lacklustre performances on Saturday, said: "I feel just like I did yesterday, but I'm not losing my title like this, I am a fighter."
